verdicts.evidence: repro/C2-verify/checks.sh (output in checks.out): grep for fleet-agent|/api/fleet|apps/fleet in AGENTS.md, apps/backend/AGENTS.md and trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md returns nothing; apps/fleet-agent/ has no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. The AGENTS.md:15-39 first rule lists only docker restart/compose, deploy.sh, rsc fleet release, /relogin and configs/sessions. The Map (AGENTS.md:43-50) has no apps/fleet-agent row. Yet apps/fleet-agent/README.md:3-8,58,108,114 says the agent starts, restarts and replaces Facebook workers to the ERP's desired count, that every start is a Facebook login (FLEET_STAGGER_SECONDS), and that `docker rm rs-fleet-*` brings a held worker back. apps/backend/src/routes/fleet.ts:151-152 mounts /hosts and /releases.
verdicts.reason: The login rule and the Map really omit the ERP-driven fleet path. Its login traps are written down only in apps/fleet-agent/README.md, and no agent doc points there. P2 fits: this is doc drift in an area the repo itself ranks as its top risk.

verdicts.evidence: apps/backend/src/routes/facebookPool.ts:680 calls PUT /v1/workers/{id}/session through callFacade, :689 calls POST /v1/workers/{id}/restore-session, and :694 calls POST /relogin. Lines 681-687 treat any 4xx from the seed (a console without the route answers 404) as mode='password', so the Assign falls back to a password Re-login. rs_console serves both routes (trackers/facebook/rs_console/rs_console/app.py:281 and :360). The 'Forwarded today' list in trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md:45-77 and the contract row at AGENTS.md:72 mention neither route nor facebookPool.ts (grep in checks.out). Coverage exists only in apps/backend/tests/facebook-pool.test.ts, which the contract row does not cite.
verdicts.reason: The contract docs are incomplete in exactly the way claimed. If the console drops or reshapes those routes, every assign silently degrades into a password login, which the code itself confirms. Severity stays P2.

verdicts.evidence: Railway MCP, read-only, project recycle-erp-experiment. list-services shows both pg-r2-backup (3224fca5) and db-sync (006cd405). get-service-config: pg-r2-backup has rootDirectory /backup and configFile /backup/railway.toml, with R2_* and DATABASE_URL variable names. db-sync has no production config; in dev it uses rootDirectory deploy/railway-sync, cron 0 4 * * *, and PROD_DATABASE_URL/DEV_DATABASE_URL variable names. backup/README.md:3 and backup/railway.toml:1 still name the backup service `db-sync`, and no doc in the repo says `pg-r2-backup`.
verdicts.reason: The misnaming is real and checked against the live service names. It is a docs-only misdirection with no effect on whether backups run or on data, and someone looking up the service on Railway sees both names plus the root directory. That is narrow maintainability, so P3 rather than P2.
